item.title: AI-enabled Digital Transformation for Small and Medium‑sized Enterprises (SMEs)
item.content:encoded:
Yao Shi, University of North Carolina Wilmington

Lukas R. G. Fitz, Brandenburg University of Technology Cottbus – Senftenberg

Fanny-Eve Bordeleau, Dalhousie University

Claudia Pelletier, Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières

Judith Gebauer, University of North Carolina Wilmington

Small and medium-sized enterprises face significant barriers to adopting artificial intelligence-enabled technologies and digital transformation, including limited financial resources, technological access, data infrastructure, and skilled workforce capacity. This gap threatens to widen the digital divide between large organizations and SMEs, with implications for economic competitiveness, equity, and sustainability across regions and sectors.

This topical collection seeks research contributions addressing how SMEs can effectively adopt, implement, and benefit from AI technologies. The collection welcomes theoretical, empirical, design-oriented, and interdisciplinary research exploring opportunities, challenges, strategies, and outcomes of AI-enabled transformation in the SME context, including case studies and best practices that can guide organizational development and policy.

All submissions must fit the scope of Electronic Markets, a leading journal in information management and information systems. Both quantitative and qualitative research are welcome, with double-blind peer review applied to all contributions.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI adoption drivers, strategies, and readiness models for SMEs
  • AI barriers, challenges, and failures for SMEs
  • Skill gaps, workforce development, and organizational learning for AI in SMEs
  • Ethical and societal issues surrounding AI in SMEs
  • Case studies of AI adoption in SMEs and business ecosystems
  • AI innovation ecosystems inclusive of SMEs
  • Design of SME-suitable AI artefacts
  • SME practitioner perspectives on AI
  • Human-centered AI for SMEs
  • AI-enabled business model innovation in SMEs
  • AI governance frameworks for SMEs
  • AI-driven shifts in SME strategies
  • Development and management of AI ecosystems for SMEs

Timeline

  • September 15, 2026: Open for submissions
  • March 15, 2027: Submission Deadline

item.title: Digitalization for responsive and circular supply chains
item.content:encoded:
Haozhe Chen, Iowa State University

Marcel Papert, University of Bamberg

Alexander Pflaum, University of Bamberg

Günter Prockl, Copenhagen Business School

Modern supply chains face unprecedented disruptions and resource scarcity, requiring transformation from linear models to circular and responsive systems. Digital technologies—including IoT, AI, digital twins, blockchain, and platforms—are essential for achieving resilience, flexibility, and sustainability while closing material loops.

This special issue seeks research on how digital innovations support responsive and circular supply chains, including technology-driven solutions and associated business models. Contributions should address opportunities and barriers to digitalization across multiple supply chain tiers or dyadic relationships in various industries.

The journal welcomes diverse methodologies including conceptual, qualitative, and quantitative research with managerial implications. Submissions may examine automotive, chemicals, food, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, or mining contexts.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digital technologies and supply chain responsiveness
  • AI and machine learning in supply chains
  • Digital twins for products and supply chains
  • Blockchain and smart contracts in logistics
  • Digital platforms in supply chain management
  • Circular economy and supply chain sustainability
  • Product-service-systems and servitization
  • Supply chain resilience and agility
  • Supply chain visibility and transparency
  • Data ecosystems and R-strategies
  • Human-machine interaction in AI-supported supply chains
  • Cyber security in digital supply chains
  • Legal compliance in circular supply chains
  • Supply chain governance and relationship management
  • Industry-specific digital transformation

Timeline

  • October 15, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Critical Perspectives on Digital Platform Ecosystems: Governance, Influence, and Consequences
item.content:encoded:
Chayanin Wipusanawan, University of Passau

Andreas König, University of Passau

Jan Krämer, University of Passau

Hemant Bhargava, University of California Davis

This special issue examines digital platform ecosystems and their multifaceted effects on economies and societies. As platforms increasingly mediate work, communication, information access, and public participation, understanding their design, governance, and regulation becomes essential. The collection invites scholarly work addressing both the innovative potential and the societal challenges posed by these powerful intermediaries.

The special issue welcomes theoretical and empirical contributions employing diverse methodologies across information systems and related disciplines. Research may explore governance mechanisms, competitive dynamics, innovation structures, content moderation, equity concerns, regulatory frameworks, and platform effects in different economic contexts. All contributions undergo double-blind peer review.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Platform Governance and Ecosystem Orchestration
  • Strategic Conduct, Market Power, and Competitive Dynamics
  • Innovation, Complementor Dynamics, and Value Co-creation
  • Content Governance, Speech, and Public Discourse
  • Societal Risks, Safety, and Equity
  • Regulation, Policy, and Institutional Change
  • Platforms and Socio-Economic Development

item.title: Artificial Intelligence-based Assistants and Platforms
item.content:encoded:
Rainer Schmidt, Munich University of Applied Sciences

Rainer Alt, Leipzig University

Alfred Zimmermann, Reutlingen University

The Topical Collection on Artificial Intelligence-based Assistants and Platforms focuses on assistant systems (e.g. chatbots, recommenders) that are based on artificial intelligence and the interaction with users via declarative natural-language interfaces. They are present in various forms as well as industries and often assume a platform logic when services and devices from different providers are included.

The Topical Collection relates to a minitrack at the Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS) and comprises research on novel methods, models, processes, and approaches related to the design, implementation, deployment, operation, and optimization of AI-based assistants and platforms for the digital economy.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Design, implementation, and deployment of AI-based assistants and platforms
  • Novel methods and models for AI-based assistants (e.g., chatbots, recommenders)
  • Natural language interfaces and user interaction with AI systems
  • Platform logic and integration of services from different providers
  • Operation and optimization of AI-based assistants and platforms for the digital economy
  • AI-based assistants in various industries and applications

  • Invalid DateTime: Submission deadline

item.title: Digital Transformation and Service
item.content:encoded:
Christian Bartelheimer, University of Göttingen

Daniel Beverungen, Paderborn University

Sara Hofmann, University of Agder

Lysanne Lessard, University of Ottawa

This topical collection examines how digital technologies reshape organizational value creation through a service lens. The collection seeks research that integrates digital transformation and service perspectives within information systems, moving beyond surface-level claims to investigate how IT artifacts fundamentally enable, constrain, or transform service exchange and value co-creation across organizational boundaries, platforms, and ecosystems.

The collection welcomes diverse research methodologies including design science, qualitative studies, quantitative research, and literature reviews. Studies are particularly encouraged to examine real-world service scenarios in inter-organizational contexts such as service networks, digital platforms, and business ecosystems, with attention to how digital technologies shape customer relations, value propositions, and service delivery.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digital transformation
  • Service systems and ecosystems
  • IT artifact design and application
  • Value co-creation
  • Customer relations and service exchange
  • Digital platforms and data spaces
  • Smart service systems
  • Information technology in organizations
  • Generative AI and large language models
  • Digital responsibility

item.title: Service research in the digital era
item.content:encoded:
Cristina Mele, University of Naples Federico II

Francesco Polese, University of Salerno

Jim Spohrer, International Society of Service Innovation Professionals

Bård Tronvoll, Karlstad University

Digital transformation has fundamentally reshaped business and society, creating new opportunities for service research. The collection explores how technological advances including artificial intelligence, augmented reality, internet of Things, blockchain, and automation enable value co-creation and market transformation. Service research conceptualizations must adapt to reflect the increasing role of technology in shaping how companies, communities, and societies function.

Markets can be understood as service ecosystems where multiple actors—both human and non-human—engage in value co-creation. Technological adoption generates opportunities for market emergence, market shaping, and institutional change, while also presenting challenges that continually transform service contexts. This collection invites research examining how technology influences service dynamics across diverse industry settings and market structures.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Service research and digital transformation
  • Human-machine interactions and robots in value co-creation
  • Technologies as enablers of market emergence and transformation
  • Technologies and market shaping and market viability
  • Phygital customer journey and metaverses
  • Service research in complex industry settings
  • Business models to manage networks and service systems
  • Emergence and institutionalization in service eco-systems
  • Application of service-dominant logic to networks and markets
  • Advances in combining network theory and service science
